cust-lucy: Hi — after onboarding via Okta SCIM + client_credentials our integration can call /embeddings and /rerank fine but generation endpoints return 403. Example response: {\"error\":\"insufficient_scopes\",\"missing\":[\"generate\"]}. Any quick triage steps?

 tom: Sorry about that — can you paste a redacted access token (first/last 8 chars) or the decoded claims? Also which flow created the token (client_credentials / auth code)?

 cust-lucy: client_credentials from Okta app. Redacted token: eyJ...abcd1234. Decoded payload shows: 
```
{"iss":"https://okta.acme.com","sub":"svc-app","aud":"redwood","exp":1712349999,"iat":1712346399,"scp":"embeddings rerank"}
```
No "generate" in scp.

 maya: That matches the 403. Our runtime enforces a scoped entitlement named "generate" (used for chat/text-gen). If scp claim doesn't include it we'll reject generation requests. Two common Okta pitfalls:
1) Okta app-role/group mapping adds roles to `roles` claim instead of `scp`
2) Token service (client-credentials) isn't configured to include custom scopes in `scp` for machine-to-machine grants.

 tom: Can you repro quickly with curl so we have the exact server log? Something like: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...abcd1234" \ 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-1","prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response should be 403 + JSON from auth layer. Paste server error id if present.

 cust-lucy: Pasted output: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "insufficient_scopes", "missing": ["generate"], "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d" }
```
Our Okta admin says the access token contains only app roles and scopes configured per the app settings.

 maya: Quick workaround: create a Console API key from the org (Settings -> API Keys) and use that for generation until IdP mapping is fixed. Longer term: ask your Okta admin to either: 
- Add a custom scope named `generate` to the Okta authorization server and ensure the client_credentials grant includes it, OR
- Map the app-role to a scope claim `scp` with value `generate` (Okta transform in Claims -> Add).

 Example Okta claim transform (Authorization Server -> Claims -> Add claim):
```
Name: scp
Include in: Access token
Value type: Expression
Value: concat("", claims.scp, " generate")  # or map role -> generate
Condition: if user.memberOf contains "redwood-gen" then true
```

 tom: I'll open an internal ticket to add a short note in our SSO onboarding doc and a troubleshooting hint for missing `generate` scope (link to Okta claim config). For now, can you confirm who the Okta admin is so we can coordinate?

 cust-lucy: Okta admin is @alex-idp. We'll ask them to add the claim. Thanks.

 triage-bot: Ticket created: CS-2026 - Okta client_credentials token missing `generate` scope for tenant acme-corp. Assigned to engineering-triage.

 maya: If you want, paste the token audit log (Okta -> System Logs) for the client_credentials issuance and we can confirm which rule is omitting `generate`. Happy to review with Alex if helpful.

 cust-lucy: Will do, thanks — will follow up once Alex updates the claim mapping.
